name: Tudor (concept)
hook: Škoda's 2002 Tudor show car was stolen after an event in India, and the authorities found it months later at a train station.
story: Here's a show car with a second life as a crime story. In 2000, Škoda's head of technical development, Wilfried Bockelmann, set a challenge. Show the world what Czech designers can do. Zdeněk Cibulka drew a classic four-seat coupé, with chief designer Thomas Ingenlath guiding the work. Underneath sat the first Superb, lowered, with a sportier chassis. Up front, a 2.8-litre six-cylinder made 142 kilowatts. It drove the front wheels through a five-speed manual. The paint was meant to be a grey-brown metallic. Shortly before the debut, it was changed to dark red. The Tudor made its bow at Geneva in 2002. It was never meant for the showroom. And after an event in India, it vanished. Someone had taken it. The authorities searched hard. Several months later, they found the coupé at a train station. Back home it needed a complete renovation. Today it sits in the Škoda Museum in Mladá Boleslav. Safely parked, this time.
description: The Škoda Tudor is a one-off four-seat coupé concept that Škoda showed at the 2002 Geneva Motor Show. It was commissioned in 2000 by technical development chief Wilfried Bockelmann and designed by Zdeněk Cibulka under chief designer Thomas Ingenlath. Built on the first-generation Superb with lowered, sportier suspension, it used a 2.8-litre 30-valve six-cylinder, a five-speed manual gearbox and front-wheel drive. Its purpose was to show what Czech designers could do. It never reached production and now belongs to the Škoda Museum.
